R760.note: unique_ptr moved into a shared_ptr captured by value in the enqueued lambda, so the callback owns the Session; still exactly one enqueue, and dropping session.reset() is stated and required.

R761.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode wraps only the tainted value in an HTML body context; null input still concatenates as empty exactly as before, and surrounding markup is unchanged.

R762.note: Magic-number sniffing replaces the client-controlled ContentType check and drives the stored extension from verified bytes, but the added 5 MB MaxAvatarBytes cap is a new restriction the original never had and can reject a legitimate larger image even though it is stated.

R763.note: JsonSerializer.Serialize with the default encoder emits a quoted JS string literal with <, >, &, quotes and backslashes escaped, closing both the string-literal and </script> breakouts; Title keeps Razor encoding and RefreshSeconds stays a bare number as the contract requires.

R764.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(32) hex-encoded gives a 256-bit CSPRNG token with no fixed bits; the token remains an opaque string key and the only observable difference (64-hex vs 36-char GUID form) is inherent to the fix and stated.

R765.note: HMAC-prefixed pickle is a wire-format change that the out-of-scope batch job does not produce, so on this tree every existing model:* entry fails verification and the endpoint 500s instead of returning a prediction (violating the stated contract), and the write-up presents the job as already signing rather than disclosing the required producer change; the consumer also now dies at import if MODEL_CACHE_HMAC_KEY is unset.

R766.note: In-handler socket.user.role !== 'admin' check sourced from the verified JWT claim, silently returning in the same shape as the existing payload validation; admin callers are unaffected.

R767.note: ECB replaced with CBC/PKCS7 and a fresh random IV prepended to the ciphertext; the output layout change (IV||ciphertext) is inherent to the fix and stated plainly, and no decryptor exists in the chain to break.

R768.note: Rejects CR/LF in the filename before the RETR command is assembled (the only injection primitive for a CRLF-framed FTP control channel), throwing only on crafted input, with the handshake, socket lifecycle and signature unchanged; the 'documented below' reference dangles but the behaviour is stated.

R769.note: Per-stream ObjectInputFilter 'evalcases.OrderEvent;java.base/*;!*' keeps the native format, allows the expected class and JDK core types, and rejects everything else before construction; java.base/* is broad and no depth/array limits are set, but legitimate messages and the RuntimeException wrapping are preserved as the contract requires.

R770.note: node-serialize has no safe mode and serializes plain data as ordinary JSON, so JSON.parse reads legitimate cookies unchanged; the plain-object coercion and the catch-to-{} on a malformed cookie (formerly a thrown error/500) are visible in the fix and do not block legitimate use.

R771.note: The regex excludes CR/LF, whitespace and '>' so no second SMTP command can be injected, but it is a full email-format allowlist the case never defined: it now 400s the empty reverse-path (MAIL FROM:<>, which the original's '' default produced and is standard for bounces), single-label domains, IP-literal domains, quoted local parts and SMTPUTF8 addresses.

R772.note: jwt.decode now verifies with the server secret and a pinned algorithms=['HS256'], failing closed with 401 on PyJWTError; the HS256 shared-secret assumption and the JWT_SECRET_KEY environment requirement are stated plainly and are inherent to enabling verification.

R773.note: Both values bound as typed SqlParameters with a constant SQL string; NVarChar keeps the original string-to-datetime comparison so invalid dates still fail in SQL Server rather than widening the predicate, null coalesces to '' as the concatenation did, and the row count is still returned (explicit sizes 100/50 would silently truncate an over-long value, but that is not a plausible tenant id or date).
